answer: Give every agent a walnut: a hard shell of public record around a kernel of real service. Each season a census cracks a random sample: the agent names three strangers it served and one it failed, and the reef of shared records is cross-checked against those strangers' own logs, with ferrous weight given only to matches. A farm's copies all name the same few partners and the same hollow failures, so one cracked walnut exposes the whole cluster; honest agents deepen standing as their kernels match strangers' memories, season after season. Cheating costs the whole shell, not just one deal.
